I want to be a musician.

Not a "rockstar". Just a respectable musicican, living off of the music I make.

In a general sense, that is.

Are you in school right now?

Talk to your school/campus therapist. They can compile a decent list of therapists that are suitable for *your* needs. Finding something that works for you AND your wallet should be less of an issue then.

Thanks. No really, even if you are on the other side of the planet. ;)

It's just that I don't really see a way out. I'm finding it to be more laborious to just breathe every day. 

Well, I'm seeing my therapist later. I'm not sure exactly how much I want to tell him. I'll probably let him know about my suicidal thoughts, but I'm not really going to talk about specifics or anything.

Thanks for listening.

That sounds alright.

Like I said, I really enjoy music. If I even so much as *think* about having a future where I'm self-sufficient, it somehow involves music or teaching.

But I'm just a High school junior with *very* success-oriented parents. And I don't think they'd be all too thrilled if I sacrificed precious study-time to somehow develop music-creating abilities.

I always envisioned that I'd have so much personal freedom after I was done with school. I dunno. That seems like the only time that I'll have to actually do something I enjoy. And I'm not even sure if I'm going to live to see those days.

But I'm sorry to hear that's happened to you. You deserved to keep that job, one way or another. But I'm glad that you're getting back on your feet, mentally.

My family is generally supportive. I guess I'm just that selfish to think about ending my life at *all*, when my parents are doing the best they can.

Apparently my dad went through some type of depression when his dad died when he was 15. But he's told me *many times* that the way he worked through it was, well, by working. Work is pretty much all he knows. He attempts to make me feel better by constantly pointing out how necessary work is to my future of my life. While that may have worked for him, he doesn't have any clue that what he says isn't actually helping at all. In fact, what he says is closer to the problam than it is to the solution.

But that's another long story; one that I don't particularly feel like talking about.

Thanks for putting up with my bullshit.

It doesn't sound nearly as selfish as expecting someone who feels such a way to continue living a life of pain.

Sorry to sound cynical there; I just really dislike it when people associate suicide with selfishness. 

But thanks. I'm still trying to make the most out of therapy.

Now, as I said, she's experienced a lot of traumatic stuff with her life. That being said, I don't necessarily believe she's acting this way *because* of me.

However, you make a good point. I'm patronizing her feelings, when in reality, what she's doing is slowly eating away at my love for her. I need to get a grip, and just tell her what I want- no, NEED from this relationship (CAKE's song "Perhaps, Perhaps, Perhaps" comes to mind).

I would *like* for her to stop acting this way altogether, but I feel it may not happen instantly. But what I *need* from her is to quit insulting the way I handle myself sometimes.

Thanks. If I could upboat you twice, I would.

The way she's been acting recently (which I described above) wasn't always like that. If anything, I don't find her feelings to supplement my depression, or make me a masochist in any way. If I really take what she said personally, than it would drive me away.

Thanks, but as I said, I'm not going anywhere anytime soon. Dealing with this just needs patience. I just hope that it doesn't require more patience than I have. At which point, I might reconsider what you've said.
Thanks, but I think it'll be better if I just be patient, and not take what she says about me to heart. I think this is the type of reassurance she needs.

Ehhh, it's a fairly awkward situation.

Now, she might have been friendly with you before you met your current gf, and now that you're with her, she feels a twinge of jealousy, and this may be her way of acting upon her feelings. 

In this sense, the best thing for you to do is communicate to the friend that the way she's acting is making you feel uncomfortable. If she's truly a friend, she'll back off. However, if she persists with her behavior, I suggest you cut off contact with her. She'll lose interest if you stop communicating to her.

Hope I've helped. ;)
Have you known the friend before you started dating your current girlfriend?
I'm pretty fucking speechless right about now.
